title: The understanding agents: a decomposer, a map reviewer and a data-need agent behind validators, the coordinator's map state, and the map on Home that the person edits and confirms
request: Phase 2 of the owner's plan: an agentic system that understands a problem, breaks a complex one into parts, and shows the big picture to the person who can change it; adoptable by the main product.
spec: dclab_core.mapping (the three roles, the reviewer's rules, the coverage of the data card, the person's edits), the coordinator's map state, the ledger points map.size and map.edit, dclab_rnd.draft.map and its routes, the panel on Home, and a measurement of the roles against the rules (dclab_rnd.agent_eval.complex, gate map_gate_v1).
plan: Roles that read the person's words but write nothing a leak could come from: what decides one is the rules' to give.
A model's question advises and never blocks; the rules' soundness check does.
The person edits the map and every edit is checked, refused with its reasons and recorded as a move and a decision.
Measure the roles against the rules on written problems, with the gate fixed first and a sealed set run once.

decisions.decision: A model draws parts, families, reads and steps; the rules supply labels, the moment of each prediction and when an outcome is known.
decisions.why: Those three decide whether a sub-problem may read another's outcome; a model that writes them can write the leak the validator exists to catch.

decisions.decision: A rule template may be named only if the rules found it in the person's words.
decisions.why: Otherwise a model can add a fraud part to a churn question by saying fraud.

decisions.decision: A problem of several parts is built only from a map the person confirmed, in the coordinator and in the build route.
decisions.why: The same gate everywhere: never built while a blocker is open.

decisions.decision: A stale map that holds nothing of the person's is drawn again; a map the person edited or confirmed is never undone by new words.
decisions.why: New words must not let an old reading through, and must not throw the person's work away.

decisions.decision: The plain arm of the measurement reads the role's own reply.
decisions.why: The same sample of the model, compared with and without the checks, at half the cost.

change: dclab_core mapping.py and three prompts (new), coordinator.py, ledger.py, problem_map.py, agents, conformance, schemas and CHANGELOG 0.51.0; dclab_rnd draft/map.py, draft/api.py, draft/coordinator.py, ledger capture, models settings and routing, harness roles, the Home page; agent_eval/complex and evidence/campaigns/map_roles_v1; tests test_mapping, test_draft_map, test_complex_measure and the changed ones.

findings.defect: A circular import between the contracts, the problem map and the new roles module.
findings.scenario: Importing the problem map first failed when the contracts' tail imported the roles module before the map had defined its classes.
findings.cause: The contracts registered the roles module at their end; either module may be imported first.
findings.fix: The roles module registers its contract from the end of the problem map, after the map is defined.
findings.test: test_decision_models ImportTest (every module imports first in a fresh interpreter)

findings.defect: The map decisions were silently not recorded.
findings.scenario: map.size was refused: the ledger's state is a closed vocabulary and had no field for parts or template; the quiet writer skipped it.
findings.cause: A decision site written before its state fields existed.
findings.fix: The state fields parts, parts_before, parts_after and template were added with the points.

findings.defect: The map route answered 500.
findings.scenario: The advisor for the three roles asked the gateway about purposes that were not declared.
findings.cause: The purposes, the role list and the understanding set were not extended with the roles.
findings.fix: The three purposes, the harness roles and the understanding set; a data-limit test for each.

findings.defect: A model's questions collapsed into one.
findings.scenario: Fifteen different questions of one kind about one part were deduplicated to one because they shared the code of a model's question.
findings.cause: The same-question test compared codes.
findings.fix: Two questions are the same when their text is, or the rule's own code about the same thing.

findings.defect: Removing the parts of a map one by one stopped half way.
findings.scenario: After the first two removals a fusion was left with one input and the budget step mixed a ride with an account: every further removal was refused.
findings.cause: A removal kept the shape of the steps.
findings.fix: A fusion or gate left with one input is dropped, its output becomes that input and its key goes to the step that now meets the units.

findings.defect: A need for a file of known cases was met by the main table.
findings.scenario: With one main table and no file of cases, the known-cases need fell back to the main table and nothing said the cases were missing.
findings.cause: The table finder always fell back to the only main table.
findings.fix: A known-cases need is a labels table or nothing; only the rules' own needs may assume the main table.

findings.defect: The page showed a placeholder as a fact.
findings.scenario: A moment 'how long after is a question to ask' was shown under Needed, and every part repeated the whole sentence as its reason.
findings.cause: The templates wrote a moment the person had not given, and one reason for all parts.
findings.fix: No moment is written when the words give none (the reviewer asks once for all parts) and each part says why it is there.

findings.defect: A problem of several parts now needs one confirmation before a build, and two flows changed with it.
findings.scenario: The fraud Home tests and the owner's morning (RG-01) built straight from the answers; their words say fraud, so a map is drawn and confirmed first.
findings.cause: The build gate is the design: never built while a blocker is open.
findings.fix: The tests confirm the map as the person does; RG-01 expects the two steps draw_map and confirm_map and nothing else changed.

findings.defect: A live run was cut at its token limit and stored as unscored.
findings.scenario: Two runs failed on their first request at 1300 tokens: the model reasons before its JSON.
findings.cause: The limit was set from the size of the JSON alone, and a second request a case doubled the cost bound.
findings.fix: The plain arm takes the role's own reply (one request a case, the same sample of the model) and the limit is 2500, a bound under half a euro.

findings.defect: Done-when not met as written on the dev run: the roles were worse than the rules on two cases.
findings.scenario: MAP-001: CD-01 and CD-03 lost; their gold had the linked-accounts part the words never mention, and CD-07, the same shape, had none.
findings.cause: The dev gold followed the template's always-include-rings assumption while the prompt told the model not to invent parts.
findings.fix: The prompt lets the model keep the parts of the rules' template that fit, naming it; Done-when is restated as the gate (no size regression, at most two worse); the plain arm is shown beside the gate; the dev gold is kept and its disagreement named.

findings.defect: A step naming a dropped sub-problem read another's id.
findings.scenario: Two ungrounded sub-problems dropped and the rest renumbered: a budget step then took the classifier instead of the review list, and validate accepted it.
findings.cause: A name that was not renamed was kept as it was, and spN is a valid new id.
findings.fix: Every spN in a step is renamed or dropped, never read as another's.

findings.defect: The model wrote what the person did not say, and what decides a leak.
findings.scenario: A churn question plus a part 'rule: fraud' became a complex map; known_rank 1 let an outcome read pass the validator; labels 'column' suppressed the reviewer's questions.
findings.cause: A rule name was checked against the vocabulary only; ranks, labels and outcomes were taken from the reply.
findings.fix: A rule is named only if the rules found it; the moment of a sub-problem follows from what it reads, labels and the late outcome come from the rules' own reading of the same family, an outcome is kept only as the person's words.

findings.defect: A table the data card does not hold was not dropped, and a leak suspect was accepted.
findings.scenario: A need for phone_calls became rides[fare]; final_customer_fare was accepted for the screen; the test that should have said so asserted nothing.
findings.cause: The table finder fell back to the only main table for a model's name, and the parse took any column of the table.
findings.fix: A model's table is an exact or word match only; a column the data card suspects of leaking is never taken.

findings.defect: The build gate ignored a map drawn from fewer words.
findings.scenario: A single map drawn for a first sentence; the person then said fraud, and the build went through unconfirmed.
findings.cause: The gate and the coordinator's facts read the stored map without asking whether it was stale.
findings.fix: A stale map that holds nothing of the person's is treated as not stored, and is drawn again when the map is asked for.

findings.defect: Drawing the map again was an unaudited change of state, and a string 'false' redrew it.
findings.scenario: A redraw dropped the person's edits and confirmation with no graph move and no decision; the body {redraw: 'false'} was truthy.
findings.cause: The redraw returned early and the flag was read as truthy.
findings.fix: A redraw is a graph move and a map.edit decision of the person; only a JSON true redraws.

findings.defect: Edits crashed with 500 and could be spoofed.
findings.scenario: A unit over 120 characters, a non-text unit, a long key or a twenty-first part raised a validation error; a body key such as draft_id raised a type error; a client-sent 'who' was kept as the author.
findings.cause: Limits were checked by the contract only, and the body was spread into the call.
findings.fix: Over-limit and non-text values are refused edits; the body keeps the edit's own keys; the author is always the person.

findings.defect: A single map could not be corrected on the page, and a confirmed map was dropped without asking.
findings.scenario: A misread complex problem showed no controls; 'Draw it again' dropped a confirmed map at once; the reviewer's unit and moment questions had nowhere to be answered.
findings.cause: The panel drew controls for complex maps only.
findings.fix: A single map shows its questions, 'Add a part' and 'Draw it again'; drawing again asks first; the questions say they are answered in the chat.
findings.test: the page, checked in the browser at desktop and phone width

findings.defect: Smaller defects: lost concurrent edits, reused ids, adopted moments, wrong joins.
findings.scenario: Two edits at once overwrote each other and a confirm could bring a removed part back; ids were reused after removal; a merge gave a part the other's moment; a new part always joined the first fusion; the sealed-run test would fail after its one run.
findings.cause: An edit read the map outside the draft's update.
findings.fix: One update reads, checks and writes; removed ids are never reused; a merge needs equal unit and moment; `into` names the step; the sealed test says at most once; the decomposer's purpose names the unit and moment it is shown.

findings.defect: The setting that switches the roles on was not documented.
findings.scenario: The gate's config test failed: DCLAB_MAP_ROLES is read by the code and was in no example file.
findings.cause: The switch was added with the code and the example file was not.
findings.fix: It is documented in .env.example with its safe default (off).

findings.defect: The measurement's records lacked the keys every other suite's records carry.
findings.scenario: The Lab page lists every campaign's results by experiment_id and status; the new results had neither and its test failed.
findings.cause: The writer was written before the page's reading was looked at.
findings.fix: The writer adds experiment_id, status and completed_at, as the other suites do, and the five records written so far got the same three keys (unpushed, so no registered evidence was changed).

measurements.name: the decomposer against the rules on the dev problems
measurements.gate: On the sealed set of 14 problems: a mean families F1 with the roles above the rules', no case whose size the rules had right and the roles got wrong (0), and at most 2 cases scored lower than the rules; written before any run, read on the sealed set, so a dev run is shown for development only.
measurements.result: Dev set of 14: mean F1 0.9381 with the roles against 0.7381 with the rules, size right in 13 cases against 10, worse than the rules in 2 cases (CD-01 and CD-03: the fraud template's linked-accounts part, which their words never mention) and better in 6, no size regression; the plain arm on the same replies scored 0.9381.
measurements.next: Run the sealed set once, at the end of the phase, and switch the roles on only if the gate passes.
measurements.against_gate: Mean F1 0.9381 against 0.7381; size regressions 0 against 0; cases worse 2 against 2.
limits: Fourteen problems written by the same hand that wrote the rules' templates: two golds follow the template, not the words.
One run of a model that is not deterministic: another run may differ by a case.
The plain arm reads the same reply, so it shows what the checks cost on that sample, not what a second sample would say.

outcome: A complex problem is drawn as parts and shown on Home with the reason for each part and the reviewer's questions; the person removes, merges, adds and confirms, every edit checked and refused with its reasons; a problem of several parts is not built until the map is confirmed; the roles read the person's words through validators, and on the dev problems they scored above the rules.
lessons: What decides a leak is never the model's to write: give it the structure and take the facts from the rules.
A gold written from a template measures the template: say which cases disagree with the words.
A model that reasons before its JSON needs a limit set from the worst case, and the run that fails is stored, not scored.
A gate that holds a build needs a way through it that the person can use in the page, with its reason.
A closed vocabulary that a quiet writer skips fails silently: test that the record exists.
risks: The roles do not serve until their sealed run passes; until then the rules draw and review.
The gate holds the build of a problem of several parts until a person confirms; a false template match costs one click.
The programme of linked projects is 24.5: until then the build below the map is for the problem the card names.
